sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Private Investment Holding for High-Net-Worth Family Assets

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-national tax or legal distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: civil law base (Latin/Spanish tradition codified in the Codigo de Comercio and Codigo Judicial) with substantial Anglo-American corporate law influence; Ley 32 de 1927 is modeled on common-law corporation statutes; commercial and maritime law practice follows strong English common-law principles.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1985)
Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement, Investment Chapter (in force 31 October 2012)
Double Taxation Agreements (selected, OECD-aligned): Panama-Mexico, Panama-Luxembourg, Panama-Barbados, Panama-Spain, Panama-Portugal
Tax Information Exchange Agreements concluded with OECD member states under the Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information

Multilateral Conventions applicable: Hague Apostille Convention (1961), UN Convention against Corruption, and OECD Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (as a non-member signatory context)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on the Prevention of Money Laundering, Terrorism Financing and the Financing of the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction, as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019 and subsequent amendments; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 51 de 14 de julio de 2016 mandating the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (UBO register) held by the licensed resident agent; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 363 de 21 de diciembre de 2017 regulating the licensing and supervision of resident agents; Acuerdo No. 5-2015 of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panama (customer due diligence and AML/CFT obligations for banking and securities custody activities); Resolucion No. 1 de 2018 of the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF) issuing reporting and identification standards; corporate foundation law: Ley No. 32 de 1927, Ley General de Sociedades, and Ley No. 1 de 1984 (Ley de Fideicomiso).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), director, officer and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of citizenship or residence of the individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) affixed by the competent authority of the issuing state; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization by a Consulate of Panama abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized sworn statement of source of wealth and source of funds (declaracion jurada de origen de fondos y de riqueza)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the UBO's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: General corporate Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent, and special Power of Attorney for incorporation purposes
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the grantor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization by a Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and certified excerpt of the shareholder registry for any legal entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations, BVI Registry, or Panama Registro Publico)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, resident agent clients, UBOs and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HMT Financial Sanctions Target List, and the domestic UAF list of persons subject to preventive measures and politically exposed persons (PEPs). The screening must be performed at onboarding, at the 10% ownership threshold, and continuously on an event-driven basis. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for the Private Banking Wire and Securities Custody payment rails, including independent verification of identity, physical address, source of wealth, source of funds, underlying family structure, and the commercial rationale of the Single Family Office. The protocol aligns with FATF Recommendations 10, 12 and 25, and Acuerdo 5-2015 (SBP) on CDD, PEP treatment, and record-keeping for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama, Direccion de Personas Juridicas, via the electronic portal eReg (Registro en Linea) available at the official website of the Registro Publico; name clearance is obtained through the 'Vale de Nombre' procedure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish and English are both accepted in practice. Non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must include the corporate form designation 'Sociedad Anonima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.', must not duplicate exactly or be confusingly similar to an existing registered name or pending Vale, and must not misstate the entity's legal form, nationality, or regulated status. Names in a foreign language are permitted when expressed in Latin characters, but authoritative Spanish equivalents are recommended for banking counterparties.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A Vale de Nombre may be renewed for one additional 30-day period upon payment of the registry tariff. Upon rejection, the resident agent or applicant may either (a) refile an alternative name, which is the commercially fastest remedy, or (b) file a written administrative reconsideration (recurso de reconsideracion) before the Direccion General del Registro Publico within five working days of the written denial, followed by an administrative appeal (recurso de apelacion) to the higher authority of the Registro, and ultimately judicial review before the appropriate Civil Circuit Court (Juzgado de Circuito en lo Civil) of the First Judicial District in accordance with the Codigo Judicial. All appeal submissions must be prepared by a duly licensed Panamanian attorney.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. Ley 32 de 1927 requires every Sociedad Anonima to maintain its registered office at the physical office of a licensed resident agent domiciled in Panama. A pure virtual office consisting only of a mail-forwarding address is not recognized for statutory purposes and will be treated as a red flag by Panamanian private banks and securities custodians. However, the SFO may legitimately use the licensed resident agent's physical office as the registered office without leasing separate commercial premises in Panama, provided that actual management, board decision-making, and asset-holding substance are documented and can be demonstrated to counterparties under the territorial tax regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate. The licensed resident agent is subject to routine and unannounced inspections by the Superintendencia de Bancos and the Unidad de Analisis Financiero, with approximately 10-15% of resident agent firms examined per annual supervisory cycle. The Single Family Office holding vehicle itself, being an unlicensed passive investment holding company, carries a quantified annual risk of direct physical inspection of less than 5%; this risk rises materially toward and above 50% if the entity engages in unlicensed financial intermediation, holds third-party funds, or maintains custody assets without an appropriate regulated service provider.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the incorporation deed (Escritura Publica de Constitucion)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed and corporate books in the Registro Publico de Panama
Licensed resident agent, first-year professional fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate services provider (agente residente) in Panama City

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register creation and AML/CFT client due diligence file (Ley 23 de 2015, Decreto Ejecutivo 51 de 2016)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for AML file preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization fee bundle (passports, powers of attorney, bank references, corporate extracts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: MICI, Registro Publico, Panamanian Consulates, and foreign competent authorities under the Hague Convention

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, name risk review, and SFO structuring opinion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed or hourly rate for single-family-office structuring

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and public translation of the corporate Power of Attorney and supporting declarations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 2 de febrero de 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas), as amended by Ley No. 6 de 2007 and Decree-Law No. 2 de 2010; Articles 3 (incorporation formalities), 4 (name requirement), 19 (registered office and resident agent), 30 (capital and shares), and 42 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Pacto Social y Estatutos) — protocolized before a Panamanian Notary Public and filed for inscription in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The corporation must issue at least one share; authorized capital is stated in the Escritura Pública (commonly USD 10,000) and is subject to registry stamp fees only. No escrow or deposit of capital is required at incorporation. A single-family office capital structure of 10,000 common shares with no par value is standard.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A.

WHEREAS: The Company was duly incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Panama pursuant to the Escritura Pública registered in the Public Registry under Entry No. [X];

IT IS RESOLVED:

1. The issuance and subscription of the registered common shares by the founding shareholders are ratified and duly recorded in the Share Register.

2. The registered office of the Company is established at the Resident Agent's address in Panama City, Republic of Panama; statutory books and the Share Register shall remain at this address.

3. [NAME] is appointed President, [NAME] is appointed Secretary, and [NAME] is appointed Treasurer, each serving until successors are elected.

APPROVED AND ADOPTED this [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Online Certification Module, Sede Electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search request to the Public Registry's certification module to verify that the proposed corporate name (ending in 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima') is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered or reserved entity. Obtain the official Certification of Name Search (Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre) as a prerequisite to notarization. Provide two alternative names in the application to avoid re-filing if the first preference is rejected.
required_dossiers: Name search application form signed by the instructed incorporator
Public Registry fee payment order
Instruction letter from incorporators to local counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is reserved by a third party or deemed confusingly similar, file a reconsideration brief with the Public Registry Name Section within the objection window or immediately submit the alternative name for a new search; name priority follows date of filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Escritura Pública
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública del Circuito de Panamá (Notary Public of the Judicial Circuit of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the single-family office object clause (exclusively investment holding and administration of the founding family's assets), authorized capital, share classes, indefinite duration, board structure, and mandatory resident agent clause. At least two incorporators (natural or legal persons) must appear before the notary, execute the deed, and pay the protocolization stamps. The deed must appoint the Resident Agent and state that the Corporation waives any inventory requirement where lawfully permitted.
required_dossiers: Passport or cédula copy and tax identification of each incorporator
Draft Pacto Social y Estatutos in Spanish prepared by counsel
Certification of Name Search from the Public Registry
Letter of acceptance from the appointed Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects or omissions, the deed is returned for amendment and re-execution before the same notary; no registry penalty is incurred if the corrected deed is re-filed before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Company at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the protocolized Escritura Pública to the Mercantile Section together with proof of payment of the registration fee calculated on authorized capital. The Registry conducts a compliance review against Ley 32 de 1927 and, upon approval, issues the Inscripción (folio real) evidencing the corporation's legal existence and recording the Resident Agent and initial directors.
required_dossiers: Protocolized original of the Escritura Pública (notarial certificate)
Payment receipt for registry fees and fiscal stamps
Certification of Name Search (verified by Registry during review)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registry issues a 'razón de objeción' or clarification note, the incorporator or counsel must submit a corrective brief or an amended deed within the notified term; failure to cure within 30 days results in archival of the filing without prejudice to re-presentation with new fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC) at the General Directorate of Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – e-Tax Portal (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica/Registro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the Registry inscription, apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) through DGI's e-Tax platform. The corporation is classified as a resident entity subject to territorial income taxation; voluntary registration in the ItBMS (VAT) system is required only if the SFO conducts taxable activities — typically none for pure passive holding. Obtain the corporate tax ID, e-signature, and activation of the taxpayer ledger for annual financial statement filings.
required_dossiers: Inscripción certificate from the Public Registry
RUC application form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyentes)
Notarized identification of the appointed legal representative
Certified registered office declaration or lease agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI issues a correction notice or requests additional documentation, respond through the 'Solicitudes y Avisos' section within 15 days; the RUC remains blocked until all compliance conditions are satisfied and the file is activated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice (Aviso de Operación) and Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección General de Desarrollo Económico (Ventanilla de Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación to classify the single-family office's physical presence as an administrative office dedicated exclusively to internal family-asset holding and wealth management. The Municipality issues the operating notice certification and enrolls the company in the municipal tax roll. This notice is not an industry license and does not authorize banking, commercial trust, fiduciary, or third-party asset-management activities.
required_dossiers: RUC tax ID certificate from DGI
Public Registry Inscripción certificate
Lease agreement or certified property title of the Panama office
Written activity description confirming exclusive single-family office passive scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality assigns a commercial activity code mischaracterizing the SFO as a financial intermediary, submit a written reconsideration with the corporate purpose excerpt demonstrating the passive holding character and absence of public solicitation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Statutory Records, Officer Appointment Protocol and UBO Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian law firm or trust company)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the Libro de Actas (minute book), Registro de Acciones (share register), and execute the First Board Resolution appointing officers. Issue share certificates to the beneficial family trust or individual holders. Prepare the UBO (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) file for CRS/AEOI and AML due-diligence record-keeping and adopt the corporate governance minutes approving internal control procedures consistent with the SFO's medium-risk enhanced classification.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution signed by the initial directors
Share subscription list and share certificate stubs
KYC/UBO identification forms for each ultimate beneficial owner
Physical or digitized statutory minute book and share register folios
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Resident Agent identifies an incomplete UBO witness chain, complete supplemental KYC documentation within 5 business days; failure to maintain an accurate UBO register may result in the Resident Agent refusing to certify accounts or issue good-standing certificates.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – no sectoral industrial license applies to a passive single-family holding vehicle; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) license and Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV) authorization are expressly not triggered absent commercial banking, fiduciary services, or securities intermediation to unrelated third parties.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – the municipal Aviso de Operación (administrative office classification) is the sole operational predicate; no banking, insurance, capital-market, or trust license is required for a strictly internal family-asset holding company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category I – low significance): office-only occupancy with no industrial processes, no stationary combustion sources, and no hazardous waste generation; an EIA registration (Informe de Categoría I) is triggered only for physical fit-out exceeding MiAMBIENTE construction thresholds, otherwise no filing is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewerage standards of IDAAN and D.L. No. 2 de 1997 (Regulación Sanitaria de Aguas Residuales); zero VOC generation from production activity; electronic and paper records destroyed through licensed waste operators with retention of disposal manifests in accordance with Ley No. 41 de 2007; structural and occupancy compliance per municipal building regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by SINAPROC (Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil) covering fire extinguishers, egress markings, and occupancy load; structural load verification per the Panamanian Building Code and Reglamento de Construcción Sostenible; workplace hygiene and occupational health clearance from MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral) where staff are engaged; compliance with NFPA 101 occupancy limits and municipal zoning approval for office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); tax registration and return portal: SIPT – Sistema Integrado de Pagos Tributarios (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/SIPT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Sociedad Anónima obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) as follows: (i) complete notarial S.A. incorporation and inscription in Panama's Public Registry; (ii) appoint a Panamanian resident registered agent and, if necessary, a fiscal representative; (iii) file the RUC application with DGI on Form 800 or through the SIPT official electronic registry, attaching certified incorporation documents, Public Registry certificate, registered-agent consent letter, passport/ID and beneficial-ownership declarations, and proof of registered office; (iv) receive the RUC and automatic ITBMS/withholding registration; (v) activate SIPT digital credentials and, if applicable, apply for e-certificates to engage in facturación electrónica. Foreign legal persons without Panama-source income or permanent establishment are not required to obtain a Panamanian RUC solely by reason of share ownership in a Panama S.A.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope; Tax_Exempt_Zone (only under Panama Pacifico, Colón Free Zone, or qualifying SEM/Multinational Headquarters regime); standard S.A. is not Pass_Through_Eligible.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a U.S.-style 'check-the-box' pass-through election. Mandatory entity-level taxation applies. Available statutory elections include: i) consolidated Panamanian income tax filing for a group that can satisfy the 100% direct/indirect shareholding and prior DGI authorization test; ii) the SEM (Multinational Headquarters) regime under Law 41 for qualifying SFO service hubs; iii) Panama Pacifico/Colón Free Zone fixed-tax incentive contracts; iv) simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime for turnover at or below B/.36,000 per year. No hybrid mismatch or transparent-entity election is available for a Panamanian S.A.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (value-added transfer tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (Balboa/USD) of annual gross turnover; all persons habitually performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama above this threshold must obtain ITBMS registration. Persons with turnover at or below the threshold may elect the simplified 'pequeño contribuyente' regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama's DGI has mandatorily phased in electronic invoicing ('Facturación Electrónica'). Affected taxpayers must issue invoices through DGI-approved systems connected to SIPT via REST APIs using XML/JSON payloads, authentication digital certificates, QR code, and digital stamp; the DGI performs real-time fiscal clearance/validation before the invoice is legally effective. Paper invoices with fiscal seals remain only during transition/complement. Non-compliant invoices cannot be used to claim input ITBMS or income-tax deductions by the SFO.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS 0% is available for: i) tangible goods that are definitively exported from Panamanian customs territory; and ii) services rendered by Panamanian taxpayers to non-resident persons for use/exploitation outside Panama. The SFO must title the export invoice to the foreign family entity/bank, retain customs exit proof for goods, document the non-resident use/location of services, and evidence the receipt of payment from abroad. The zero-rated supply also carries a right to refund of accumulated input ITBMS attributable to such export activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) validated by Panama's Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas, including customs clearance number and exit confirmation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical shipment and departure of goods from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT/telex confirmation evidencing receipt of export consideration from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, and the underlying sale or services contract describing the destination and offshore use
For exported services: DGI-compliant invoice, service agreement, and technical evidence of use/benefit outside Panama
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits match export declarations, transport documents, and banking credits; incomplete or abusive zero-rating documentation will be recharacterized as taxable Panama-source revenue, evaluated at 7% ITBMS plus accrued interest and monthly surcharges. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims can trigger fines from 50% to 200% of the omitted tax, nullification of refunds and credits, clawback of previously recovered input tax, disqualification from customs facilitation status, and criminal liability for tax fraud (Law 14 of 2010 and Fiscal Code penalties). The ordinary DGI assessment period is generally five years from the relevant filing date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Banco Nacional de Panamá (not an issuing central bank); Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (macro-fiscal oversight); Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for AML/Sanctions enforcement
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized with the Balboa at a nominal 1:1 parity to the US dollar; US Federal Reserve notes are legal tender. No exchange controls, no foreign-exchange licensing obligation, and no differentiated current-account versus capital-account regime. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and outbound transfers execute freely in USD without central-bank approval or convertibility delay. Tax withholding and reporting requirements continue to apply under Panamanian territorial taxation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender period, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no hard-currency repatriation requirement applies to export receipts earned by a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima. Export proceeds may be retained offshore, credited to beneficiary accounts in Panama, or reinvested without exchange-control filings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Private Banking Wire Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for unlicensed offshore digital EMIs. Panama does not recognise the EU EMI passport and SBP licensing is required for deposit-taking, banking, and regulated payment services. An SFO should not hold any material liquidity with a non-bank fintech EMI; only locally licensed fintech institutions under Law No. 1 of 2024 (Innovación Financiera) or a fully licensed SBP bank may serve as a compliant clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interviews are generally required. For a corporate SFO, the beneficial owner(s) and at least one authorised managing officer must physically appear before the bank's compliance officer during onboarding and at each material change in control. Remote opening is accepted only in narrow exceptional cases and requires enhanced video due diligence, a licensed introducer, and immediate notarised documentation delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or obscured beneficial ownership through Panamanian private interest foundations (PIF) or trust layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust or PIF charter, current registered beneficial-owner schedule, notarised passports of settlor and ultimate beneficiary, certificate from registered agent, corporate registry excerpt, and a formal source-of-wealth narrative signed by the responsible officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-net-worth asset flows without auditable source-of-funds narrative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the SFO (if established), original bank statements from upstream institutions, executed sale/purchase contracts, income tax filings, legal fee letters, inheritance documentation, and a certified public accountant's asset-origin report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, sanctions-list, or adverse-media exposure of the family principal, director, or authorised signatory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official PEP declaration and mitigation questionnaire, vendor sanctions/PEP screen result from Thomson Reuters or LexisNexis, national reference letters, central criminal record certificate, passport and residence permits, plus an explicit written explanation of any politician-family or state-enterprise affiliations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto-currency, gambling, or unexplained round-trip payment history on upstream accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete digital-asset exchange audit trail, certified wallet signatures, disposition certificates confirming liquidation, anti-crypto declaration affirming future cessation, and forensic accountant explanation for every round-trip or split payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections route via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) through the Panama beneficiary bank's correspondent relationship with a US clearing bank. The beneficiary Bank Identifier Code (BIC) and Panama-specific bank-charge account number must be provided; Panama uses 9-digit bank account identifiers and does not use IBAN. No central-bank permission or purpose code is mandatory; however, the SFO should ensure the payment reference contains the covert corporate name, account number, and 'Capital Contribution – Escrow' to assist AML screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for supplier payment, SWIFT MT202 for interbank clearing and nostro prefunding, and UCP600-compliant commercial letters of credit issued by Tier-1 Panamanian banks for goods and services. Domestic disbursements may use Panama's local automated clearing house (ACH Las Nubes) and real-time low-value rails for Balboa/USD settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR deliverable forwards and FX swaps
Fully collateralised cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) offered by top-tier global correspondent banks
FX options on major currencies under ISDA 2002 with approved credit support annex

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI / ANIP), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year irrespective of fiscal year-end; no ordinary extension available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest accrues at 10% per annum; the company is unable to obtain a clearance certificate (paz y salvo) for commercial transactions; non-payment for three consecutive years may trigger administrative strike-off and liquidation by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Annual Return (pure equity holding company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI / ANIP), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the close of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, filing is due by December 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Graduated fines under Law 70 of 2019, up to USD 50,000 for failure to file or for inaccurate filing; recurrent non-filing may lead to administrative restrictions, including prohibition on registration acts and public disclosure of non-operational status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 101/LC) – required only where Panamanian-source taxable income exceeds statutory thresholds or the company is formally registered as a taxpayer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI / ANIP), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end; thus, for calendar-year taxpayers, due on or before March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at 10% per annum plus graduated fines ranging from 5% to 50% of the tax due depending on the period of delay; unpaid or un-filed returns may also block issuance of tax clearance certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to licensed financial or insurance entities, public-interest companies listed with the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores, and any corporation whose annual gross taxable revenues exceed USD 1,000,000 or whose accounting capital exceeds the regulatory threshold set by the DGI; a passive single-family office holding entity does not fall within the mandatory audit requirement unless one of these thresholds is triggered.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Panama, or NIIF para Pymes (IFRS for SMEs) for smaller entities; financial statements are generally maintained in USD because of Panama's dollarized economy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2020 and Executive Decree 214 of 2021, every Sociedad Anónima must maintain an internal beneficial-ownership register at the office of its registered agent. There is no central annual UBO filing for a non-regulated private holding company; however, the resident agent must perform an annual KYC refresh and any share transfer must be recorded in the company's share ledger and the beneficial-ownership register updated within 30 days. A formal annual confirmation to the agent is part of the standard client acceptance and anti-money laundering protocol.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 750 per year for a full-service Panama registered agent with corporate secretary support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not generally required for a passive family-office holding entity; if an audit is triggered, a certified audit typically ranges from USD 2,500 to USD 7,500 depending on asset complexity and consolidation needs.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama's territorial tax system generally taxes only Panama-source income. Foreign-source income of a Panamanian corporation, including capital gains from offshore sales and dividend income from non-Panamanian entities, is outside the scope of income tax. A Single Family Office (SFO) holding passive foreign investments can structure its affairs so that effectively no Panamanian corporate income tax applies to foreign-source investment returns. Domestic-source income, if any, is subject to the 25% standard corporate rate. Certain taxpayers qualify for preferential regimes, but standard SFO holding activities do not automatically qualify for a statutory tax holiday; instead, the territorial exclusion is the operative incentive.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02 (Declaración de Renta) for legal entities; filed via DGI's electronic portal 'Sede Electrónica' (www.dgi.gob.pa) or the integrated 'E-Tax' system of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following tax year. Payments of the final assessed tax are due with the return; estimated payments during the year are governed by rules for corporations with taxable domestic income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identificación del Contribuyente: tax identification number (RUC - Registro Único de Contribuyentes) of the Panamanian corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SFO's Panamanian S.A. must register for a RUC with a resident agent (agente residente) and include the RUC on the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Período fiscal: tax year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the annual accounting period elected by the entity; commonly January 1 to December 31 unless a different fiscal year was approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos brutos totales: total gross revenue; for an SFO, includes dividends, interest, capital gains, and other investment income sourced from Panama and abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panama-source income is taxable. Foreign-source income should be reported separately in the corresponding foreign-source income schedule, if required by DGI; otherwise it may remain excluded from taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos exentos / no sujetos: income that is exempt or outside the territorial scope, such as foreign-source portfolio earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the excludable character of each foreign-source income item. Maintain bank and broker records establishing that income was generated outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos y gastos deducibles: deductible costs and expenses attributable to the generation of Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where no Panama-source income exists, allocate no local expenses to taxable activity. Management fees paid to directors or the SFO's officers are deductible only if they relate to taxable Panama-source income and meet arm's-length and formal documentation requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta gravable (base imponible): taxable income after exemptions and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure foreign-investment SFO, this line will typically be zero. If any Panamanian bank deposits generate Panama-situs interest, that interest is Panama-source and taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto sobre la renta causado: resulting income tax at the 25% rate (or applicable lower rate for listed domestic-source income categories).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the territorial rule scrupulously. Interest earned on deposits with a Panamanian bank is Panama-source and subject to tax, though a final withholding regime may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Créditos, retenciones y pagos a cuenta: creditable withholding taxes, credits, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any Panamanian tax withheld, e.g., final withholding tax on local dividends or local interest. Do not claim credit for foreign taxes withheld abroad, because foreign-source income is excluded from Panama tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto a pagar o saldo a favor: net tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If territorial exclusion eliminates taxable income, the amount due should be zero or a refund/credit carried forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaración jurada: sworn declaration signature of the legal representative or resident agent, with public accountant certification where required by DGI thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident agent must ensure timely filing even if tax is zero; failure results in fines.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fines range from USD 50 to USD 5,000 depending on gross receipts, plus 1% monthly interest on unpaid tax. Failure to file may also trigger an administrative assessment and suspension of the RUC or inability to obtain a 'Paz y Salvo' tax clearance. A 10% surcharge applies to tax paid late beyond the statutory deadlines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% over the taxable dividend distribution to individuals or non-resident shareholders; distributions of previously taxed profits bear a reduced 4% dividend withholding tax (dividend tax paid out of the corporate income tax). A 5% rate applies to dividends paid from profits subject to a preferential regime. Internal group dividends to non-resident parent companies may qualify for a 0% withholding rate if paid from profits already subject to Panamanian tax and the distribution is not deductible by the payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's double tax treaty network is limited (most treaties are with Caribbean and Central American jurisdictions). To invoke a reduced withholding rate under an applicable DTA: (i) obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the treaty counterparty's tax authority; (ii) present the TRC together with Form 630 (or the specific withholding tax form) to the Panamanian withholding agent before the distribution; (iii) complete and deliver Form 670 or equivalent to DGI within the withholding payment period; (iv) maintain documentary evidence of beneficial ownership of the dividends, interest, or royalties. For jurisdictions without a treaty, treaty relief is unavailable and the statutory rate applies. Panama applies automatic exchange of information (CRS and FATCA) regardless of treaty status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident creditors is generally subject to a 6% to 12.5% withholding tax depending on the character and source; the standard rate for cross-border interest remittances to non-bank foreign beneficiaries is 12.5% unless a treaty reduces it. Royalties paid to non-residents for use of intellectual property or technical assistance are subject to a 12.5% withholding tax (25% for certain technical services). Under the reduced treaty provisions, rates may be capped at 5% for royalties and 5%–10% for interest, but Panama's operational network makes such relief rare.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 2,000,000 (USD 2,000,000) of annual related-party transactions or gross income above that threshold triggers mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File under Executive Decree No. 56 of 2014 and DGI Regulation 4-2014).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not currently levy a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime for SFOs. However, the General Directorate of Revenue and the Superintendency of Banks apply substance-over-form, and an SFO must demonstrate actual substance in Panama to preserve territorial tax benefits, avoid recharacterization as a laboratory of concealment, and satisfy its resident agent's 'know your client' duties. Having a local office, local board decisions, accounting records kept in Panama, and a Panamanian bank account are critical. The 2015 Law No. 52 on legal entities requires Panamanian corporations to maintain their accounting records in Panama and to present them to the resident agent upon request; failure to do so results in loss of legal personality or fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Non-Filing of Territorial Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panamanian SFO to hold assets and report zero Panamanian tax while failing to file annual Form 02, failing to register with the RUC, or deliberately mischaracterizing Panama-source income (e.g., interest from Panamanian private banking accounts) as foreign-source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under the Tax Code of up to 100% of the omitted tax, adjusted penalties, interest at statutory rates, and criminal tax fraud sanctions in aggravated cases. In suspension or revocation of the corporate status (reforma de la sociedad) for failure to comply with resident agent obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is available under Panamanian law where fraud or abuse is proven. Directors and the resident agent may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes. Criminal tax evasion can lead to imprisonment (up to 5 years), travel bans, and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an 'offshore' holding vehicle with no Panamanian office, no local books, no local decision-making, and no commercial rationale; failing to maintain accounting records in Panama as required by Law 52 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines; involuntary dissolution; prohibition of judicial acts; adverse tax residency determination by foreign tax authorities under CFC or substance rules (e.g., U.S. GILTI, EU ATAD); negative impact under the risk-based market entry of international banking compliance standards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations or knowingly permit the entity to act as a bare shell may face personal liability for resulting fines, civil restitution to creditors or investors, and criminal exposure for fraud. Directory removal and travel bans can be imposed in the context of money laundering investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Private Banking Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Single Family Office to move funds through private banking wire rails and securities custody without declaring the underlying beneficial owner to the resident agent, without conducting AML/KYC due diligence, or knowingly handling proceeds of foreign corruption or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama's AML Law (Law 23 of 2015, expanded by Law 70 of 2017), fines range from USD 10,000 to USD 5,000,000 per violation. The UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) may suspend accounts, and criminal money laundering carries 10 to 15 years imprisonment. Panama is a CFATF member; serious deficiencies can trigger countermeasures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, nominee shareholders, and resident agents who are aware of suspicious transactions without filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (RFS) are personally liable. Criminal liability includes imprisonment, pecuniary fines, travel bans, and confiscation of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to disclose ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) to the resident agent and, where applicable, to the DGI or Registry's beneficial ownership database; using bearer shares prohibited after the 2015 reforms; having nominee directors without a formal declaration of the principal's patrimonial control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and sanctions from the Superintendency of Companies and the DGI; refusal to provide Paz y Salvo; cancellation of registration; consequences under international tax transparency standards for being non-compliant with beneficial ownership data (Executive Decree 207 of 2015).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominee director who exercises formal control without written instructions from the beneficial owner is exposed to civil liability for unauthorized transactions; the true owner may be barred from asserting ownership rights; custodial criminal penalties may be applied in case of fraudulent vehicles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty/DTA Abuse and Tax Clearance Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming treaty withholding relief in a DTA jurisdiction by submitting a false TRC; asserting non-residence before foreign authorities while simultaneously managing the company's affairs from within Panama for Panamanian-source investment management service fees; creating phantom related-party transactions to shift profits out of Panama at below-arm's-length prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reversal of treaty benefits, gross-up of withheld taxes, penalties of 50% to 100% of the under-withheld amount, and criminal fraud charges under the Tax Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute false certificates or who direct improper treaty applications may be subject to personal fines, civil indemnification for tax liabilities, and, in aggravated cases, up to 6 years of imprisonment for forgery or fraud, plus travel bans.
